papers.title: Combining multimodal fatigue fracture surface images for analysis with a CNN
papers.abstract: This work uses three different modalities, namely SEM, BSE and scanning white light interference (SWLI) to image fatigue fracture surfaces of Ti-6Al-4V. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that were pre-trained on images of the natural world were used to predict values such as distance from load line and crack growth rate. SEM images are routinely used to study the topography of fracture surfaces because the shallower interaction volume resolves surface features while BSE images and SWLI data add information about composition and surface height. Combining the three imaging modalities via the use of color channels facilitates overlaying them on the same grid for transferability of models pre-trained on colored images. This work shows that the imaging modalities under the guise of color channels have different levels of importance depending on the model being trained. It also documents how the combination of information from these modalities improves the classification and regression results by 20 and 60 %, respectively, relative to the secondary electron images alone. (162/200).

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文使用Ti-6Al-4V疲劳断口表面图像开发多模态CNN，但未直接提供增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的力学或疲劳性能数据。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on a multimodal CNN image analysis method for fatigue fracture surfaces rather than on the mechanical or fatigue characterization of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V itself.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用多模态图像改进疲劳断口表面裂纹扩展率的预测能力。
summary_zh.method: 将SEM、BSE和SWLI图像作为颜色通道输入预训练CNN。
summary_zh.result: 多模态组合较单模态图像回归精度提升60%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过对比单模态结果验证多模态效果。

summary_en.motivation: To improve the prediction of crack growth rate from fatigue fracture surfaces by leveraging multimodal imaging data.
summary_en.method: SEM, BSE, and SWLI images were combined as color channels and fed into a pre-trained convolutional neural network.
summary_en.result: The multimodal approach improved regression performance by 60% compared to using secondary electron images alone.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed by comparing the multimodal model's predictions against single-modality results.
